title: Championship Round 3 - Biblical Mysteries & Intellectual Frontiers
description: 50 high-difficulty questions: 25 Bible Knowledge + 25 General Knowledge.

questions.question_text: Which king of Israel was killed by Zimri while recovering from wounds inflicted by the Syrians?
questions.explanation: Zimri conspired against Elah and killed him while he was drinking in the house of Arza, his palace steward.

questions.question_text: Who was the father of Bezalel, the chief craftsman appointed to construct the Tabernacle?
questions.explanation: Bezalel was the son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was instructed to purchase a linen waistband, hide it near the Euphrates, and later retrieve it ruined?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah's ruined waistband symbolized Judah's pride and its loss of usefulness through disobedience.

questions.question_text: Who killed Sisera by driving a tent peg through his temple?
questions.explanation: Jael struck Sisera while he was sleeping in her tent after he fled from Barak's army.

questions.question_text: Which priest discovered the Book of the Law during the repairs of Solomon's Temple under King Josiah?
questions.explanation: Hilkiah discovered the Book of the Law and handed it to Shaphan the scribe.

questions.question_text: Which son of Gideon escaped the massacre of his brothers at Ophrah?
questions.explanation: Jotham, the youngest son of Gideon, hid himself and survived Abimelech's massacre of his seventy brothers.

questions.question_text: Which prophet rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of relying on the Lord?
questions.explanation: Hanani the seer confronted Asa and declared that his reliance on Syria rather than God was foolish.

questions.question_text: Which man was appointed to oversee the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls and served as governor?
questions.explanation: Nehemiah led the reconstruction of Jerusalem's walls and served as governor of Judah.

questions.question_text: Which prophet saw a vision of a basket of summer fruit symbolizing the end of Israel's opportunity?
questions.explanation: The basket of summer fruit represented the ripeness of Israel for judgment.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was commanded to name his daughter Lo-Ruhamah?
questions.explanation: Hosea's daughter Lo-Ruhamah symbolized that God would no longer show mercy to the house of Israel in the same manner.

questions.question_text: Who was the father of John the Baptist?
questions.explanation: Zechariah was a priest of the division of Abijah and the husband of Elizabeth.

questions.question_text: Which disciple was also known as Didymus?
questions.explanation: Thomas was called Didymus, a name meaning twin.

questions.question_text: Who was the mother of King Lemuel, whose instructions are recorded in Proverbs 31?
questions.explanation: Proverbs identifies the speaker as the words of King Lemuel, taught to him by his mother, without naming her.

questions.question_text: Which prophet foretold that the Messiah would be born in Bethlehem Ephrathah?
questions.explanation: Micah prophesied that a ruler over Israel would come from Bethlehem Ephrathah.

questions.question_text: Which Roman governor succeeded Felix and heard Paul's defense alongside King Agrippa?
questions.explanation: Festus succeeded Felix as governor and heard Paul's defense before Agrippa and Bernice.

questions.question_text: Who was the prophet that anointed Jehu as king of Israel through one of his disciples?
questions.explanation: Elisha sent a young prophet to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu as king.

questions.question_text: Which man was struck dead after touching the Ark of the Covenant to steady it?
questions.explanation: Uzzah touched the Ark when the oxen stumbled, and the Lord struck him down for his irreverent act.

questions.question_text: Which woman became the first recorded Christian convert in Europe after Paul preached in Philippi?
questions.explanation: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, received Paul's message and was baptized with her household.

questions.question_text: Which king of Judah was taken captive to Babylon with bronze chains and later released by Evil-Merodach?
questions.explanation: Jehoiachin was released from prison by Evil-Merodach and given a place above other captive kings.

questions.question_text: Who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams of seven healthy cows and seven thin cows?
questions.explanation: Joseph interpreted the dreams as seven years of abundance followed by seven years of severe famine.

questions.question_text: Which prophet was told to purchase a field at Anathoth while Jerusalem was under Babylonian siege?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah purchased his cousin Hanamel's field as a prophetic sign that land and houses would again be possessed in Judah.

questions.question_text: Which apostle was chosen by the church in Jerusalem to accompany Paul and Barnabas to Antioch with the council's decision?
questions.explanation: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas were chosen as leading men to accompany Paul and Barnabas.

questions.question_text: Which Old Testament king was instructed by Isaiah to apply a cake of figs to his boil?
questions.explanation: Isaiah instructed that a lump of figs be applied to Hezekiah's boil, after which he recovered.

questions.question_text: Which man was appointed by Moses to lead Israel after him?
questions.explanation: God instructed Moses to commission Joshua son of Nun as Israel's next leader.

questions.question_text: Which prophet saw four chariots emerge from between two mountains of bronze?
questions.explanation: Zechariah's eighth vision describes four chariots representing heavenly spirits going throughout the earth.

questions.question_text: Which phenomenon explains why a rotating black hole can transfer rotational energy to particles passing through its ergosphere?
questions.explanation: The Penrose process allows energy extraction from a rotating black hole through particle interactions within its ergosphere.

questions.question_text: Which physicist formulated the equation describing the wave function of a quantum system?
questions.explanation: Schrödinger developed the wave equation that describes how the quantum state of a system evolves.

questions.question_text: Which ancient Greek mathematician is credited with proving that there are infinitely many prime numbers?
questions.explanation: Euclid's Elements contains a famous proof that the set of prime numbers is infinite.

questions.question_text: Which battle in 1066 resulted in the Norman conquest of England?
questions.explanation: William, Duke of Normandy, defeated King Harold II at Hastings and subsequently established Norman rule in England.

questions.question_text: Which philosopher introduced the concept of the categorical imperative as a foundation of moral philosophy?
questions.explanation: Kant's categorical imperative establishes unconditional moral principles that apply universally to rational agents.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the boundary separating Earth's crust from the mantle?
questions.explanation: The Mohorovičić discontinuity, or Moho, marks the seismic boundary between Earth's crust and mantle.

questions.question_text: Which empire was ruled by Ashurbanipal, known for establishing a major royal library at Nineveh?
questions.explanation: Ashurbanipal ruled the Neo-Assyrian Empire and assembled a vast collection of cuneiform tablets at Nineveh.

questions.question_text: Which literary work by Dante Alighieri describes a journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise?
questions.explanation: The Divine Comedy is Dante's epic poem describing his allegorical journey through the three realms of the afterlife.

questions.question_text: Which scientist discovered the neutron in 1932?
questions.explanation: James Chadwick demonstrated the existence of the neutron through experiments involving beryllium radiation.

questions.question_text: Which economist wrote The General Theory of Employment, Interest and Money?
questions.explanation: Keynes published The General Theory in 1936, profoundly influencing modern macroeconomic thought.

questions.question_text: Which astronomical object is defined as a stellar remnant supported primarily by neutron degeneracy pressure?
questions.explanation: A neutron star is an extremely dense remnant of a massive star, supported against gravity mainly by neutron degeneracy pressure and nuclear interactions.

questions.question_text: Which civilization developed the earliest known extensive system of writing in Mesoamerica, often associated with the earliest monumental inscriptions in the region?
questions.explanation: The Olmec civilization is associated with some of the earliest evidence of writing and complex symbolic inscription in Mesoamerica, although the origins and attribution remain debated.

questions.question_text: Which mathematical theorem states that every non-constant polynomial with complex coefficients has at least one complex root?
questions.explanation: The fundamental theorem of algebra guarantees that a degree-n polynomial over the complex numbers has exactly n roots when multiplicity is counted.

questions.question_text: Which treaty established the European Economic Community in 1957?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Rome established the European Economic Community and Euratom in 1957.

questions.question_text: Which molecule acts as the primary electron donor in oxygenic photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Water is oxidized at photosystem II, releasing electrons, protons, and molecular oxygen during oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.question_text: Who wrote the philosophical work Leviathan, which examines the origins and justification of political authority?
questions.explanation: Thomas Hobbes published Leviathan in 1651, arguing for a powerful sovereign authority to prevent social conflict.

questions.question_text: Which scientist formulated the laws of electromagnetic induction and contributed to the development of the electric generator?
questions.explanation: Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction in 1831, establishing the principle behind electric generators and transformers.

questions.question_text: Which ancient historian wrote The Histories, a major account of the Greco-Persian Wars?
questions.explanation: Herodotus is traditionally called the Father of History for his extensive account of the Greco-Persian conflicts and related peoples.

questions.question_text: Which particle is responsible for mediating the electromagnetic interaction?
questions.explanation: The photon is the gauge boson of the electromagnetic interaction.

questions.question_text: Which empire's ruler, Mansa Musa, made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage demonstrated the wealth and influence of the Mali Empire across trans-Saharan trade networks.

questions.question_text: What is the name of the mathematical structure used in general relativity to describe the curvature of spacetime?
questions.explanation: A Lorentzian metric defines spacetime intervals and allows general relativity to describe gravitational geometry.

questions.question_text: Which novel by Mary Shelley is widely regarded as an early foundational work of science fiction?
questions.explanation: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, published in 1818, explores scientific ambition, responsibility, and the consequences of creating life.

questions.question_text: Which principle in thermodynamics states that the entropy of an isolated system never decreases?
questions.explanation: The second law states that the total entropy of an isolated system remains constant for reversible processes and increases for irreversible processes.

questions.question_text: Which civilization constructed the city of Machu Picchu in the Andes?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca civilization in the fifteenth century in the Andes of present-day Peru.

questions.question_text: Which scientist proposed the theory of continental drift in the early twentieth century?
questions.explanation: Alfred Wegener proposed continental drift in 1912, arguing that continents had once formed a larger landmass called Pangaea.
